entries.name: Adonai
entries.note: A Hebrew title rendered Lord in this verse.

entries.name: Almighty
entries.note: Corrected source citation: Almighty occurs in Revelation 1:8, not 1:18.

entries.name: Angel
entries.note: Included in Torrey’s traditional Christian index of Christ’s titles. Its connection to Christ is an interpretation of this Old Testament passage, rather than an explicit use of the name Jesus here.

entries.name: Angel of God's presence
entries.note: Included in Torrey’s traditional Christian index of Christ’s titles. Its connection to Christ is an interpretation of this Old Testament passage, rather than an explicit use of the name Jesus here.

entries.name: Angel of the Lord
entries.note: Included in Torrey’s traditional Christian index of Christ’s titles. Its connection to Christ is an interpretation of this Old Testament passage, rather than an explicit use of the name Jesus here.

entries.name: Anointing
entries.note: Image: John's teaching anointing is traditionally understood as the Spirit's presence. Acts explicitly connects anointing with the Holy Ghost.

entries.name: Arm of the Lord
entries.note: Included in Torrey’s traditional Christian index of Christ’s titles. Its connection to Christ is an interpretation of this Old Testament passage, rather than an explicit use of the name Jesus here.

entries.name: Author and Finisher of Our Faith
Author of Life
entries.note: Descriptive role: the Father has life in himself and gives life (John 5:21,26); God gives everyone life and breath (Acts 17:24-25). This label summarizes those passages. The specific title translated Author of life in Acts 3:15 refers to Jesus, not the Father; the KJV renders it Prince of life.

entries.name: Author of Scripture
entries.note: Role: A theological description of the Spirit's inspiration: human speakers and writers speak as moved by the Holy Ghost.

entries.name: Beginning of the creation of God
Builder and Maker
entries.note: Description: Abraham looks for the city whose builder and maker is God.

entries.name: Captain of the Lord's hosts
entries.note: Included in Torrey’s traditional Christian index of Christ’s titles. Its connection to Christ is an interpretation of this Old Testament passage, rather than an explicit use of the name Jesus here.

entries.name: Convicter of Sin
entries.note: Role: Jesus says the coming Comforter will reprove the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment.

entries.name: Crown of Glory
entries.note: Image: The Lord of hosts is pictured as a glorious crown for the remnant of his people.

entries.name: David
entries.note: Included in Torrey’s traditional Christian index of Christ’s titles. Its connection to Christ is an interpretation of this Old Testament passage, rather than an explicit use of the name Jesus here.

entries.name: Desire of all nations
entries.note: Included in Torrey’s traditional Christian index of Christ’s titles. Its connection to Christ is an interpretation of this Old Testament passage, rather than an explicit use of the name Jesus here.

entries.name: Dove
entries.note: Image: The Spirit descends in a form likened to a dove at Jesus' baptism; this is a visible comparison, not his personal name.

entries.name: Earnest of Our Inheritance
entries.note: Image: Earnest means a pledge or first payment. Paul describes the Spirit as the pledge of the inheritance to come.

entries.name: El Elyon
entries.note: A Hebrew title rendered most high God in this verse.

entries.name: El Olam
entries.note: A Hebrew title rendered everlasting God in this verse.

entries.name: El Roi
entries.note: A Hebrew designation reflected in Hagar’s words, Thou God seest me.

entries.name: El Shaddai
entries.note: A Hebrew title rendered Almighty God in this verse.

entries.name: Elohim
entries.note: The Hebrew word rendered God in this verse.

entries.name: Exceeding Great Reward
entries.note: Image: God speaks to Abram, identifying himself as Abram's shield and exceeding great reward.

entries.name: Father of All
entries.note: Title: Paul speaks of one God and Father of all in his appeal for the church's unity.

entries.name: Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ
entries.note: Title: The apostles bless God as the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

entries.name: Finger of God
entries.note: Image: Parallel Gospel sayings describe Jesus' deliverance work as by the finger of God and by the Spirit of God.

entries.name: Firstfruits
entries.note: Image: Paul speaks of having the firstfruits of the Spirit while waiting for bodily redemption. This is an image of present gift and future fulfillment.

entries.name: Fountain of Living Waters
entries.note: The LORD describes himself as the fountain of living waters. In John 4:10-14, Jesus gives living water; that passage describes his gift.

entries.name: Gift of God
entries.note: Description: In this setting the gift concerns the Holy Spirit. Peter rejects the idea that God's gift can be purchased.

entries.name: Giver of Life
entries.note: Role: The KJV says the Spirit quickens or gives life. This is a description of his work.

entries.name: Giver of Spiritual Gifts
entries.note: Role: The one Spirit distributes different gifts according to his will.

entries.name: God of All Flesh
entries.note: Title: The Lord names himself as the God of all flesh while declaring that nothing is too hard for him.

entries.name: God of My Praise
entries.note: Title: The psalmist appeals to the God whom he praises.

entries.name: God Ready to Pardon
entries.note: Description: Israel's prayer remembers God's forgiveness, patience, and mercy despite rebellion.

entries.name: Guide into All Truth
entries.note: Role: Jesus promises his disciples that the Spirit will guide them into all truth.

entries.name: Heavenly Father
entries.note: Title: Jesus uses this title while teaching his disciples about the Father's care.

entries.name: Helper of the Fatherless
entries.note: Description: The psalm appeals to God's care for the vulnerable. This is distinct from the wording Father of the Fatherless.

entries.name: Hiding Place
entries.note: Image: The psalmist addresses God as a place of protection and deliverance.

entries.name: Holy Father
entries.note: Direct address: Jesus addresses the Father this way while praying for his disciples.

entries.name: Husbandman
entries.note: Image: Jesus explicitly identifies his Father as the husbandman, or vine grower, in the true-vine teaching.

entries.name: Indwelling Spirit
entries.note: Description: The Spirit dwells in God's people; this label highlights his presence rather than a separate personal name.

entries.name: Intercessor
entries.note: Role: Paul describes the Spirit making intercession in believers' weakness. The role is shared with Christ in other passages.

entries.name: Jealous
entries.note: This verse expressly says that the LORD’s name is Jealous, describing his claim to undivided worship.

entries.name: Jehovah Jireh
entries.note: A name Abraham gives the place of God’s provision.

entries.name: Jehovah Nissi
entries.note: Moses names an altar Jehovah-nissi: the LORD is my banner.

entries.name: Jehovah Shalom
entries.note: Gideon names an altar Jehovah-shalom: the LORD is peace.

entries.name: Judge of the Widows
entries.note: Title: The psalm presents God as the defender and judge of widows alongside his fatherly care for the fatherless.

entries.name: Keeper of Covenant
entries.note: Description: These prayers and teachings praise God's faithfulness to his covenant and mercy.

entries.name: King
entries.note: King of Zion is a descriptive title supported by Psalm 2:6-7 and Zechariah 9:9. John 12:12-16 explicitly applies the coming of Zion's king to Jesus. These passages support the edited label King of Zion; they do not all use that exact three-word phrase.

entries.name: King of Heaven
entries.note: Title: Nebuchadnezzar praises God's heavenly kingship after his restoration.

entries.name: Last Adam
entries.note: Torrey labels this Second Adam; the KJV calls Christ the last Adam.

entries.name: Light
entries.note: Description: John describes God as light with no darkness in him. The image describes God's character.

entries.name: Lion of the tribe of Judah
Living Father
entries.note: Title: Jesus names the Father who sent him and speaks of life received through the Son.

entries.name: Living Water
entries.note: An image of the life Jesus gives, not a direct personal name. John 7:39 connects the living water with the Spirit.

entries.name: Lord
entries.note: 2 Corinthians 3:17 explicitly connects the Lord and the Spirit. Torrey also cites 2 Thessalonians 3:5.

entries.name: Lord God of the holy prophets
Lord of Heaven and Earth
entries.note: Title: Jesus addresses the Father as Lord of heaven and earth.

entries.name: Love
entries.note: Description: John says that God is love and points to the sending of his Son as its expression.

entries.name: Majesty on High
entries.note: Title: The Son is described as seated at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

entries.name: My Portion
entries.note: Image: God himself is described as the speaker's enduring inheritance and reason for hope.

entries.name: My Song
entries.note: Image: Songs of deliverance praise the Lord as strength, song, and salvation.

entries.name: One Who Hears Prayer
entries.note: Description: The psalm addresses God as the one who hears prayer.

entries.name: Only Wise God
entries.note: Title: Paul's closing praise is addressed to God through Jesus Christ.

entries.name: Our Dwelling Place
entries.note: Image: Moses' prayer describes the Lord as his people's home through every generation.

entries.name: Plant of renown
entries.note: Included in Torrey’s traditional Christian index of Christ’s titles. Its connection to Christ is an interpretation of this Old Testament passage, rather than an explicit use of the name Jesus here.

entries.name: Prince of the kings of the earth
Promise of the Father
entries.note: Description: Acts identifies the Father's promised gift with the coming Holy Spirit.

entries.name: Redeemer
entries.note: Title: Isaiah addresses the LORD as our Father and our Redeemer. This is covenantal Father language in the Old Testament. The corresponding Christ entry is retained.

entries.name: Refuge from the Storm
entries.note: Image: Isaiah praises God's protection of the poor and needy using the image of shelter in a storm.

entries.name: Renewer
entries.note: Role: Paul describes salvation through regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit, poured out through Jesus Christ.

entries.name: Righteous Father
entries.note: Direct address: Jesus addresses the Father as righteous in his prayer.

entries.name: Sanctifier
entries.note: Role: These passages speak of sanctification through the Spirit. The label summarizes that work.

entries.name: Saviour
entries.note: Title: God our Saviour pours out the Holy Spirit through Jesus Christ our Saviour. The context distinguishes the Father and the Son while describing both as Saviour.

entries.name: Seal of Redemption
entries.note: Image: Believers are sealed with the Holy Spirit until redemption. The label summarizes the seal imagery.

entries.name: Searcher of the Deep Things of God
entries.note: Role: Paul says the Spirit searches all things, including the deep things of God.

entries.name: Seven Eyes
entries.note: Image: The Lamb's seven eyes are identified as the seven Spirits of God sent throughout the earth. This follows the traditional reading of the Spirit's fullness.

entries.name: Seven Lamps of Fire
entries.note: Image: Revelation identifies seven burning lamps as the seven Spirits of God. This follows the traditional reading of the Spirit's fullness.

entries.name: Seven Spirits of God
entries.note: Revelation uses symbolic language. This index follows the traditional reading of the seven spirits as the fullness of the Holy Spirit.

entries.name: Shadow from the Heat
entries.note: Image: A companion image of God's protection in Isaiah's song, not a separate personal name.

entries.name: Shiloh
entries.note: Included in Torrey’s traditional Christian index of Christ’s titles. Its connection to Christ is an interpretation of this Old Testament passage, rather than an explicit use of the name Jesus here.

entries.name: Son of Man
entries.note: Corrected source citation: John 6:27 rather than 6:37.

entries.name: Spirit of Him Who Raised Jesus
entries.note: Title: Paul identifies the indwelling Spirit by his relation to the Father who raised Jesus from the dead.

entries.name: Spirit of Jesus Christ
entries.note: Title: Paul speaks of the help supplied through the Spirit of Jesus Christ.

entries.name: Spirit of the fear of the Lord
Spirit of the Living God
entries.note: Title: Paul contrasts ink and stone with the Spirit's writing on human hearts.

entries.name: Spirit Who Appoints
entries.note: Role: Paul tells the elders that the Holy Ghost has made them overseers of the flock.

entries.name: Spirit Who Bears Fruit
entries.note: Role: Paul names the fruit produced by the Spirit. The label describes his work in believers.

entries.name: Spirit Who Empowers Witness
entries.note: Descriptive role: the Holy Spirit gives power to bear witness to Jesus. This wording summarizes his work, rather than quoting a formal biblical title.

entries.name: Spirit Who Gives Freedom
entries.note: Descriptive role: where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. Paul describes freedom in the new-covenant context; this label summarizes that work.

entries.name: Spirit Who Gives Rest
entries.note: Role: Isaiah recalls the Spirit of the Lord giving Israel rest as God led his people.

entries.name: Spirit Who Glorifies Christ
entries.note: Role: Jesus says that the Spirit will glorify him by making known what he receives from him.

entries.name: Spirit Who Reminds
entries.note: Descriptive role: Jesus promises his disciples that the Holy Spirit will bring his teaching to their remembrance. This wording summarizes his work, rather than quoting a formal biblical title.

entries.name: Spirit Who Sends
entries.note: Role: The Holy Ghost calls Barnabas and Saul and sends them out for their work.

entries.name: Spirit Who Speaks
entries.note: Role: Jesus promises the Holy Ghost's help in speaking; Acts also records the Spirit speaking to the church.

entries.name: Spirit Who Transforms
entries.note: Role: Paul describes believers being changed into the Lord's image by the Spirit of the Lord.

entries.name: Spirit Who Unites
entries.note: Role: Believers are brought into one body by one Spirit and called to keep the unity of the Spirit.

entries.name: Star
entries.note: Included in Torrey’s traditional Christian index of Christ’s titles. Its connection to Christ is an interpretation of this Old Testament passage, rather than an explicit use of the name Jesus here.

entries.name: Strength of My Heart
entries.note: Image: The psalmist confesses dependence on God when flesh and heart fail.

entries.name: Strengthener of the Inner Man
entries.note: Role: Paul prays that believers will be strengthened by the Father's Spirit in their inner being.

entries.name: Strong Tower
entries.note: Image: The psalmist addresses God as a shelter and strong tower against the enemy.

entries.name: Teacher
entries.note: Role: Jesus says that the Holy Spirit will teach his disciples. Teacher summarizes this action rather than quoting a separate proper name.

entries.name: The LORD Is There
entries.note: The prophetic city is named The LORD is there, often transliterated Jehovah Shammah.

entries.name: The LORD My Shepherd
entries.note: Often expressed as Jehovah Rohi; a shepherd image for the LORD’s care.

entries.name: The LORD Who Heals
entries.note: Often expressed as Jehovah Rapha; the KJV says the LORD that healeth thee.

entries.name: The LORD Who Sanctifies
entries.note: Often expressed as Jehovah Mekaddishkem; the KJV says the LORD which sanctify you.

entries.name: Tongues of Fire
entries.note: Image: At Pentecost tongues like fire accompany the disciples being filled with the Holy Ghost.

entries.name: True God
entries.note: Title: Jesus addresses the Father as the only true God. Shared divine titles are not exclusive to one Person; the corresponding Christ entry is retained.

entries.name: Wall of Fire
entries.note: Image: The Lord promises to surround Jerusalem with protection and to be its glory within.

entries.name: Wind
entries.note: Image: Jesus compares birth by the Spirit to wind; Pentecost includes a sound like a rushing mighty wind.

entries.name: Wisdom
entries.note: Paul directly calls Christ the wisdom of God. Torrey also includes the poetic personification of wisdom in Proverbs 8; that connection is interpretive.

entries.name: Witness Within
entries.note: Role: The Holy Spirit bears witness with believers' spirits and bears witness through Scripture.

entries.name: Word
entries.note: The second reference is 1 John 5:7, correcting a book-name omission in the source.

entries.name: Yahweh
entries.note: The divine name YHWH, commonly represented as LORD in the KJV; Yahweh is a transliteration.
